GENERAL SECRETARY 
D. A. BUDGE 


Fifty-Seventh Annual Report 


With this report the Young Men’s Christian Association of 
the City of Montreal completes the fifty-seventh year of its 
history. 

The supreme purpose and aim of the Association has never 
changed. This must ever be kept in the foreground. The 
movement began and has continued until this day for the pur- 
pose of winning men and boys to the Christian life. With 
the experience of years its methods have changed, but it 
stands to-day, as it did in the first, for the cultivation of a 
normal Christian life in men and boys, and for their enlist- 
ment and training in Christian service. This supreme 
purpose must dominate all departments of the work. 

A condensed report of the work of the Central Branch, and 
the Railroad Branch, is included. The MeGill College Asso- 
ciation, although independent in its organization and 
management, is closely affiliated with the whole work in the 
city, and Dr. F. D. Adams, Chairman of their Advisory Com- 
mittee, is an advisory member of this Board, and your Seere- 
tary is a member of the Advisory Board of the College 
Association. 

From these reports we would eall your attention to some 
outstanding facts. The financial budgets for the past year 
have been as follows: 


Board of Directors... .. .. .. .. ..$10,404 18

All obligations on current expenses have been met, and a 
small balance stands to the credit of each department. For 
this result, especially in this year of financial stringency, 
your Directors are profoundly grateful to God. 

When this Central Building was opened seventeen years 
ago, the Association had 1070 members. ‘To-day the reports 
show that 3731 members are connected with the Association 
through its Branches. 

Your Directors are pleased to report that during the year 
they have paid off $17,035 on the mortgage indebtedness of 
the Association property, so that with the exception of a 
balance of $4875, the Central Building and the adjoining lots 
on Dorchester Street now stands free from indebtedness. 
There is a mortgage indebtedness of $9000 on the Railroad 
Branch at Point St. Charles. 

The Fairmount Young Men’s Association now becomes the 
Fairmount Avenue Branch of this Association, under the 
direction of a Committee of Management to be named by your 
Board. A suite of rooms, including a gymnasium and hall, 
locker room and baths, social room and reception and reading 
room, has been secured in a new building just erected on the 
corner of Fairmount Ave. and Mance St. The churches in 
that section are united in their desire that the Association 
should co-operate with them in work for young men and boys 
in that rapidly-growing section of our city. 

The needs of the East End of the city have not been for- 
gotten, but no solution of the problem has yet been found by 
your Board. It is hoped that during the coming year some 
opening may be found where a plan similar to that of the 
Fairmount Avenue Branch may be put into operation. 

The question of the enlargement of the Central Building 
has been constantly before your Board. The option of sale 
was not carried through on account of the prevailing financial 
stringency. The removal of the present building, and the 
erection of a new building covering the present site and the 
adjoining property, would be an ideal solution of this difficult 
problem for an up-to-date Central Building for this city, but 


4 


Syne, 


ONIGTING TVALNAD ‘WOON TVIDOS 


the expense and the difficulties involved in such an under- 
taking are apparent. To illustrate the evolution of the Asso- 
ciation plans, it will be seen that with the exception of the 
gymnasium, locker room, and reception hall, every part of 
the interior of this building has been altered since its erection 
seventeen years ago, and yet its equipment in the Physical, 
Educational, and the Boys’ Departments is altogether inade- 
quate in the light of the needs of to-day. Be assured that 
your Beard has this important issue constantly in mind, and 
is hoping for some satisfactory solution which will give this 
Association a modern building, thoroughly equipped for its 
work in the centre of our city. 

One bequest of $9000 has been received during the year 
from the estate of the late Miss Elizabeth Orkney, and we 
are advised that another friend, lately deceased, has remem- 
bered this Association in her will. 


To those who have a sense of responsibility for the disposi- 
tion of their money, the choice of channels of benevolence 
is often difficult in order that it may accomplish the largest 
practical good to the community. To such we would respect- 
fully suggest the consideration of The Young Men’s Christian 
Association. 


Ist. Because it is an incorporated body owning large prop- 
erty interests in the city, which must ever be administered by 
Christian business men, representing the various religious 
denominations. 


2nd. Because, while independent in action, it is closely 
related by affiliation and supervision to one of the largest 
organizations on this continent, and throughout the world. 
_ in promoting the highest interests of youth and manhood, and 
because it is absolutely unselfish in its line of effort, and 
includes in its objective all young men, irrespective of class 
or creed. 


3rd. Because of economy of administration from the fact 
that this work is so largely preventive in its plan, and also 
from the fact that money operates at the same time on so 
many lines, the moral, educational, physical, and social wel- 
fare of boys and men. 


4th. Because of the fact that its benefits extend to the entire 
city, and to all classes of young men by reason of its 
Branches. 


5th. Because it affords a wide diversity of objects to which 
funds may be applied according to the inclination of the 
donor, viz., towards the erection of buildings, the endowment 
of the work, for libraries, for evening educational classes for 
commercial and mechanical young men, for moral and 
religious teaching, and for the extension of the work through- 
out the city. 


6th. Because in the past five years such a large number of 
the clear-headed business men, and thoughtful far-seeing 
women on this continent have placed large sums of money 
either by gift or bequest at the disposal of this movement, 
and this has been done in many cases after careful investiga- 
tion of its methods and plans of work. 


7th. Because this City of Montreal has the honor of being 
the birthplace of this organization on the North American 
Continent, and therefore it should keep in the front rank of 
leadership, and because of the service which it has rendered 
to this community in the development of young men into 
broad-minded and aggressive Christian citizenship. 


This Board bears a relation to the work on the whole 
Canadian field in its connection with the Canadian Section of 
the International Committee whose headquarters is in 
Montreal. One-third of the time of your General Secretary 
is now given to the promotion of this work throughout the 
Dominion. During the past year, in addition to the visita- 
tion at local Canadian centres in Ontario and Quebec, and 
attendance at Canadian Conferences and Summer Institutes, 
he has made a trip from the Atlantic to the Pacific in the 
interest of special Association problems. This opportunity 
gives the Montreal Association a distinct and unique relation 
to the whole Canadian field. 

During the coming year your Board, in co-operation with 
the Committees of Management of the Branches, hope to give 
attention to the following matters: 


1. A more adequate promotion and announcement of the 
aims, purposes, and methods of the Association, and the 
securing of an enlarged financial constituency. 


2. A more adequate Committee organization, and a large 
increase in the number of volunteer workers. Greater atten- 
tion to the securing and training of men for Secretaries to 
meet the growing demands of the work. 


7 


3. The strengthening of our Religious Work, so as to more 
adequately meet the needs of the. young men of our city. 
This Association must ever be a recognized place where men 
can come to an immediate decision to become followers of 
Jesus Christ, and where they can gain the needed help in 
Bible Study, Christian fellowship, and practical service.. 


4, A study of the conditions which exist concerning the 
boys of the city, and to plan for a better adaptation of this 
work to meet that need and opportunity. 


5. The broadening of our Employment Work, so as to be of 
practical service to our business men, and also to our mem- 
bers, and to the young men who are seeking advice and help. 
This should have a place of recognition and importance in 
the social and religious work of the Association. 


6. The enlargement of our Educational Work, so as to more 
adequately meet the present needs and opportunities. The 
promotion of Educational Clubs and series of Practical Talks 
and Educational Lectures. No greater opportunity to serve 
young men, and to serve the business community, and to serve 
the nation is offered to the Association than through this 
Department. 


7. The extension of the Association activities in shops, 
factories, churches, and other points, in the lines of work 
now successfully carried on by the Association. 


8. An effort to come into closer relation and co-operation 
with other men’s movements throughout the city. 


9. A greater co-operation with the Laymen’s Missionary 
Movement, and the promotion of the missionary spirit and 
effort amongst our members. 


10. The extension of the Association work on Physical 
lines. Let the Gymnasium be the centre from which extension 
work may be carried on at various points throughout the city. 
This department should also plan to co-operate directly with 
those organizations which have for their object the promotion 
of the physical welfare of our citizens, by aiding the work 
of such Societies as the Tuberculosis League, Playgrounds 
Association, Social Service League, and Anti-Cigarette 
Society. : 


We report, with sorrow, the loss by death of the following 
subscribers during the year:

CENTRAL BUILDING 


Annual ‘Report of the Committee of Management 


The year just closed has been a gratifying one in many 
respects, and the Committee are profoundly grateful for the 
results which have been attained. 

The Reports of the various Co:nmittees appear in detail 
elsewhere, and it is only necessary here to refer to those 
features which require special mention. 

Notwithstanding the increase in the regular membership 
fee from $5.00 to $7.00 commencing September Ist last, the 
total membership stood at 2615 on April 30th, an increase of 
164 over the previous year. This is the largest. membership 
yet attained in the Central Building, and is largely due to the 
splendid work of the Membership Committee under the direc- 
tion of its able chairman. 

Special mention should be made of the Educational De- 
partment, which this year reports 533 different students, 172 
of whom were successful at the International Examinations. 
The tuition fees amounted to $2900.55, a gain of $268.45 over 
the previous year. 

The Summer Camp also had an unusually good season, with 
a total of 198 men and boys in attendance. The credit balance 
of $471.60, shown for the season’s operations, was transferred to 
the Permanent Camp Committee, liquidating the indebtedness 
on the property for equipment and maintenance. 

The Reading Room was converted into a Social Room, and 
‘the Reception Hall refurnished with rugs and mission furni- 
ture, under the direction of the Social Committee, greatly 
adding to the attractiveness of the Building. 

One of our Assistant Secretaries, the late Mr. E. J. Figgis, 
devoted his entire time to the promotion of the Religious meet- 
ings and Bible Classes, and the visitation of young men with 
encouraging results. This was a new step, and one which was 
certainly justified. 

The Physical and Boys’ Departments were well sustained 


13 


in their leading features, but we have still to report a cramped 
condition in respect to the space necessary for these two im- 
portant branches of our work in this Building. 

We regret to report the loss of the following members by 
death during the year :— 


Campbell, A. H. - - died Aug. 27, 1907. 
tamsay, J. Hale = - died Oct. 20, 1907. 
McNamara, M. J. - - died Dee. 1907. 
Riches, J.C. = : - died Feb. 6, 1908. 
Figgis, E. J. - - - \ died Mar. 21, 1908. 
Auld, R.S. L - - died April 2, 1908. 


C. C. HOLLAND, 


Chairman. 


C. K. CALHOUN,. 


Secretary.

The total membership on April 30th, 1908, was 2615, an increase 
of 164. The total receipts from fees were $10,324.40, a gain of 


$564.65 over last year.

The Committee conducted a ten-day contest, closing March 21st, 
which resulted in adding 278 new members and $1,013 in receipts. 

For the -great success that attended our efforts in connection 
with this special membership contest, the Committee are deeply 
indebted to the many friends who tendered such generous and 
hearty support throughout the movement. 


23 


LIFE MEMBERSHIP. 


The advisability of increasing the number of life members was 
seriously considered by the Committee, and consequently special 
work has been done in that direction, with the result that twenty- 
five (25) new life members have been added to the list during the 
last month. 

J. W. McCONNELL, 
Chairman. 


EDUCATIONAL DEPARTMENT 


EVENING CLASSES. 


During the school year—September 30, 1907, to March 81st, 
1908 — classes were conducted in Arithmetic, Bookkeeping, Short- 
hand, Typewriting, Penmanship and Business Correspondence, 
French, Accountancy, Mechanical Drawing, Building Construction, 
Steam Engineering, Electricity, English for non-English speaking, 
Plan Reading and Estimating, and Shop Mathematics. The last 
two are new courses. 

The following group courses were organized and successfully 
carried on: 


Engineering—Including Advanced Mechanical Drawing, Machine 
Design, Shop Mathematics, and Boiler Firing. 


Matriculation, Part I—Including Arithmetic, Grammar and 
Composition, History and Geography. 


Matriculation, Part II—(a) Mathematies — Algebra, Euclid, and 
Trigonometry. 
(b) Language—French and Latin. 
(c) Science—Physics. 


Group Course for Boys—Including Arithmetic, Penmanship, 
Business English, History and Geography. 


The total number of different students was 533, viz., 425 men 
and 108 boys. 
A comparison of the receipts and expenses and examination 
results for the past three years: 
1905-6 1906-7 1907-8

A Debating Club and a Natural Science Club were formed among 
the boys. In connection with the latter organization trips were 
taken to points in the surrounding country, and talks given on the 
growth and habits of plants and animals. 

Spring term, 1908. Classes for the spring term are being con- 
ducted in Shorthand, French, Matriculation, and Engineering. For 
the first time a summer school in Engineering is being conducted. 
The class meets two evenings per week, and is in charge of Mr. 
Peter Bain. Seventeen men enrolled.

DEBATING CLUB 


Membership, 384. The Debating Club met every Monday evening 
throughout the fall and winter. Besides the general debates and 
discussions among the members, two debates were held with other 
clubs. Addresses were given by the following gentlemen: Mr. 
Samuel Groves, Mr. Calder, Mr. Robt. Neilson, Mr. J. B. Sellars, 
Mr. Abner Kingman, Rev. Dr. Symonds. 

SETH P. LEET, 


Chairman. 


READING ROOM AND LIBRARY. 


The Library contains 5,100 volumes, 237 of which were added 
during the past year. Five hundred and thirty-five members have 
used its privileges. Nine thousand seven hundred and fifty books 
have been issued as follows:

A new members’ reception, held in the fall, was attended by 
90 boys. Mr. J. J. Virgo, of Australia, was one of the speakers. 


RELIGIOUS. 


Owing to the falling off in the attendance during the winter 
months, the Friday Night Meeting was discontinued at the end of 
January, and replaced by a similar service held fortnightly on 
Sunday morning at 9.30, alternating with the hospital service. The 
Friday Night Meeting averaged 31 boys, and the Sunday Morning 
Service averaged 26 boys. A special mass meeting, conducted by 
Mr. J. J. Virgo, of Australia, was attended by 160 boys, and was 
productive of great good. j 

The Song Service, held every fortnight at the General Hospital, 
has had an average attendance of 32 boys. 

One hundred and eighty-nine boys (44% of total membership) 
were enrolled in Bible classes during the winter season, divided 
into seven classes as follows:

27 


Eighty-five boys are using Scripture Union Cards for daily Bible 
reading. Seventy dollars has been subscribed to the boys’ work in 
Calcutta. 


PHYSICAL. 


The attendance at the Gymnasium Classes is covered by the 
Physical Report. 

A Junior Leaders Corps was organized last fall, consisting of 12 
boys who, with the Intermediate Leaders Corps of 16 young men, 
have rendered splendid and valuable service, not only to the 
physical work, but to the entire work of the department. 

Four “Open Nights’ in connection with the gymnasium were 
held, two at the commencement and two at the close of the season, 
all of which were largely attended with great interest by the parents 
and friends of the boys. 

A class conducted for those learning to swim has been held on 
Saturday morning with good results. 

The Summer Camp was held for four weeks under the leadership 
of Mr. Holliday, assisted by an efficient staff of eight leaders. The 
total attendance was 69 boys, viz.: Business boys, 28; School boys, 
41. Total, 69. As heretofore the Camp was successful in every 
respect, and helpful to many of the fellows in the development of 
Christian manhood. 

A series of indoor athletics, held by the Business Boys’ Classes, 
was conducted with good success. 

Our boys were successful last year in winning two cups for road 
and field events. These cups must be won twice in succession 
before becoming the Club’s property. They were won by us in 
competition with about eight other clubs who are members of the 
Boys’ Harrier League. 


SOCIAL. 


Sleigh drives, snowshoe tramps, carrom tournaments, and social 
evenings have been participated in by a large proportion of the 
membership. The Annual Closing Concert was attended by 300 
boys, parents, and friends, the proceeds of which, amounting to 
$35.00, go toward defraying the expenses of delegates to the Boys’ 
Conference at Silver Bay. Last summer five boys attended the 
Conference. 

The Library is well patronized, and 200 new books were added 
through a special campaign for this purpose. 


EDUCATIONAL. 


The attendance at the classes is included in the Hducational 
Report. 

Thirty-three boys from the group course class wrote on papers 
set by the International examiners. 

A Debating Club was formed from the group course class and 
successfully conducted. 

A Nature Study Club w&s organized for the summer months. 

A one-week campaign, to secure $300.00 per annum for two years, 
viz., $600.00, toward the salary and expenses of a Canadian Boys’ 


28 


Secretary, was conducted from March 21st to 26th. Six teams were 
formed, composed of 45 boys in all, who, by splendid and systematic 
canvassing, secured subscriptions amounting to $1,233.85. This 
amount was subscribed by: 


Junior members... ... .. Bah etd 2a cligtce Le 
Senior members and friends.. .. .. .. 245 
459 


Frank Findlay’s team came first with $295.00, while Norman 
Johnston did the best individual work in securing. $191.00. 

Taking the work as a whole, the results for the past year are 
encouraging. There has been a considerable increase in those 
attending Bible Classes, an increased attendance at the Hospital 
services, also the Gymnasium Classes, and prospects for the coming 
year are bright in every way. 


Respectfully ‘submitted, 


LEMUEL CUSHING. 
Chairman. 


RELIGIOUS DEPARTMENT 


The Weekly Meetings and Bible Classes have been held regularly © 


throughout the year with a large and increasing interest. This 
was due to the fact that one of the Secretaries gave nearly all his 
time to this branch of the work. 


SUNDAY AFTERNOON MEETING. 


The Sunday Afternoon Meeting opened October 4th. It was at 
first held at 3.30, preceded by a song service, and followed by the 
Bible Classes at 4.30, and tea at 5.30. The plan worked well in 
many ways, but gradually the conviction came to us that it was 
not the best. In February the old plan was resumed, the Bible 
Classes meeting at 3 o’clock, and the Men’s Meeting at 4. The 
total attendance for the 29 meetings was 3,596, an. average of 124. 

Mention should be made of the visit of the Hon. H. B. Macfar- 
land, of Washington, and Mr. Alfred E. Marling, of New York. 

We are also indebted to the Hon. William Jennings Bryan, of 
Lincoln, Nebraska, for his visit and inspiring addresses, in connec- 
tion with the Laymen’s Missionary Movement, with which the 
Association actively co-operated. These were wonderfully effective 
in placing the claims of the movement before the business men 
of the city. 

The Sunday Afternoon Meeting was also addressed by Mr. J. J. 
Virgo, of Sydney, Australia; Mr. Geo. Gleason, of Osaka, Japan; 
Mr. J. M. Dudley, International Railroad Secretary; and Mr. W. P. 
Archibald, Dominion Parole Officer, Ottawa. Apart from these the 
meetings were addressed by local pastors. 

The musical service was in charge of Messrs. Hatch and Breese. 
They were assisted by friends who kindly contributed vocal and 
instrumental solos. 


29 


i> 


BIBLE STUDY. 


A great deal of attention was given to the Bible Classes, so 
that the interest of a great many new men was enlisted. They 
opened the first week in October, the Tuesday evening classes 
meeting for tea at 6.30. They were led by Mr. D. A. Budge, Rev. 
Mr. McGougan, Mr. C. K. Calhoun, Mr. John Currie, and Mr. F. W. 
C. Meyers. The thanks of the Association are due to Rey. Mr. 
McGougan for leading a class in the study of “ Messages from the 
Prophets.” 


SUNDAY AFTERNOON BIBLE CLASSES. 


The Sunday Afternoon Bible Classes were conducted by Messrs. 
Calhoun, Holliday, Figgis, and Merritt. In February these classes, 
with the exception of Mr. Merritt’s, were merged into the Men’s 
Meeting, and the hour was changed to 4 o’clock. Special mention 
should be made of the Sunday Morning Bible Class, at 9.45, con- 
ducted by Mr. E. J. Figgis, and since his death by Mr. Philip 
Turner. The International lessons are studied. 

On Saturday evening Mr. Calhoun conducted a Teacher’s Train- 
ing Class. His special purpose was to discover and train teachers 
from amongst the members of the classes. 


THE SATURDAY EVENING MEETING. ob 


The Saturday Evening Meeting had a total attendance of 2132, 
an average attendance of 41 for the year. Good earnest work was 
done. The meetings were planned to win men for the Christian 
life and build them up in Christian manhood. Special meetings 
for prayer in this connection were held before and after the 
meeting. 


SUNDAY AFTERNOON BIBLE CLASS. 


The Sunday Afternoon Bible Class, under the leadership of Mr. 
Budge, was conducted throughout the year with good results. At 
present the class meets in the new social room, at 4 o’clock. 


SUNDAY EVENING SONG SERVICE. 


During July and August a Sunday Evening Song Service, under 
the leadership of Mr. Fred J. McKellar and Mr. BH. J. Figgis, was 
held on the steps of the Association building. These attracted 
large audiences, and were maintained with splendid interest and 
effect. } 


PERSONAL VISITATION OF MEN. 


Personal visitation was more widely followed this year, Mr. E. 
J. Figgis being specially related to this work. It was found to be 
one of the most effective means of winning the sympathy and 
interest of men. 

Early in the year the late Mr. E. J. Figgis was invited to join 
the staff with special reference to the religious work and Bible 
Classes. His removal by death, on March 29th, was a matter of 
great regret to the whole membership of the Association. 


30 


PHYSICAL DEPARTMENT 


Bach succeeding year more clearly demonstrates that both boys 
and men are feeling the need of exercise, as an aid to success in 
every walk of life. 

The regular gymnasium classes have been held during the past 
year, and, as will be seen by the following report, the interest and 
attendance has been good. 


There have been twenty-eight Class Sessions held weekly, with 
a total registration of 702, as compared with 755 last year. There 
have been 378 men and boys examined. The total attendance at 
all classes for the year is 17,121, as against 17,253 the previous year. 
Seven hundred and sixty-one Class Sessions held, with a weekly 
average of 550.

The thanks of the Association are due to Drs. F. W. Gilday, R. W. 
Craig, and A. L. C. Gilday, for their very helpful courses of Prac- 
tical Talks, given to members of the department through the winter 
months. ; 

The Physical Department also wishes to record its appreciation 
of the faithful services of Dr. F. W. Gilday and Dr. A. L. C. Gilday, 
as Medical Examiners for the past year. 


31 


The Physical Department Banquet was held on April 30th. 
Socials and banquets have been held by the different classes during 
the winter, and have stimulated great interest amongst the men. 

An attractive leaflet on the “ Value of Exercise” was issued by 
the Committee, which stimulated the interest in our work. 

In addition to the above, ten clubs have been conducted by the 
department, which report as follows: 


LEADERS. 


The Leaders Corps of the Association have co-operated most 
‘helpfully in assisting the Physical Directors to carry out the work 
of the Physical Department, and have been responsible in addition 
to this for the Leaders “At Home,’ New Year’s Reception, Practical 
Talks, and Athletic Competitions. 

This ‘year a Junior Leaders Corps was organized with ten mem- 
ae and has been doing a good work in the Junior School Boys’ 

lasses. 

This gives us now Leaders Corps in the Junior, Intermediate, 
and Senior Departments. 

The Annual Gymnastic Exhibition, on New Year’s Day, 
reflected credit upon the Leaders Corps, who were responsible for 
the programme. 

TENNIS. 


The Tennis Club had a most satisfactory year, the membership 
totalling 57, the largest in the Club’s history. The team won the 
championship of the city in the Intermediate League, winning 
seven out of eight games on the schedule. The finances of the Club 
show a credit balance of $26.00. 


BASEBALL. 


The season of 1907 may be considered a successful one with 
baseball, especially so in view of our inability to secure the use of 
the Atwater Park Grounds for home games on Saturday afternoons. 
Practising on good grounds, and playing the games upon inferior 
grounds, affected the standing in the City League. Notwithstanding 
this difficulty, six out of twelve League games were won, The out- 
look for the coming season is bright. 


FOOTBALL. 


The Football Club did not have a very successful season last 
year, owing to their inability to secure a proper place for their 
League games. The Committee worked hard to keep the men 
together, but found it difficult to get enough men to play the 
regular matches. 

The Committee regret this, as there was some excellent material 
at the beginning of the season which might have been held had the 
arrangements for the grounds been different. 


HARRIER. ~ 


In the spring and early fall the runs which took place on 
Monday and Wednesday evenings were largely attended — twenty 
men turning out to each run. 


32 


The Harrier Club conducted Handicap Road Races, entering into 
the Senior and Intermediate Independent Harrier League, took an 
active part in the King’s Birthday Road Race, and altogether had 
a most successful season. 

The Club was fortunate in securing the McGill track two even- 
ings a week for practices, and handicaps were run off successfully. 
The thanks of the Club are tendered to the McGill authorities for 
granting them the use of their track during the summer, and for 
the privilege of holding the Eleventh Annual Field Day there. This 
latter was a great success from the standpoint of attendance and 
competition. 

The membership of the Club was 47, all being runners. 


BASKETBALL. 


The Basketball Committee report the season just closed as being 
a most successful one. 

The usual Association League games have been continued with 
five senior and four intermediate teams. The Intermediate being 
won by the “ Cubs,” and the Senior by the “ Maples.” 

Senior and Intermediate Teams were entered in the Canadian 
Basketball League, and we are pleased to report having won the 
Senior Championship of Hastern Canada. In the friendly games 


with the crack Hamilton team we were not so successful, Hamilton’ 


winning both in their home game and in Montreal. 


SWIMMING AND LIFE-SAVING CLUB. 


After the turn of the year this Club was organized, and though 
small in membership, has been successful. It has now fifteen active 
members, and has been holding competitions every Friday evening. 
Next year we hope that the report will include a list of lives saved 
by members. 

The Club has been fortunate in securing as its instructor Mr. 
R. M. Zimmerman, a good swimmer, and fine instructor. Mr. 
Zimmerman is a member of the Association, and renders this 
service voluntarily. 


GYMNASIUM MEN’S BIBLE STUDY CLUB. 


This Club has met throughout the winter months, and has had 
a most satisfactory season. Thirty-two class sessions were held, 
with a total attendance of 934, an average of 29 per Sunday. 


SNOWSHOE. 


The Snowshoe Club inaugurated their season with a successful 
“At Home,” attended by 250, and after some reorganization of the 
Committee started in early and kept up late; the average 
attendance at the Men’s Tramps being 35, and the Ladies’ Tramps 
45. In the spring, just before the close of the tramping season, a 
very successful concert was held by the Club, which was largely 
attended by friends and members. 

The membership of the Club was 76, and they closed the season 
with all expenses met. 


33 


thy 


! 


BOWLING. 


Early in the season the alleys were thoroughly overhauled and 
put in excellent condition, and with the addition of new sets of 
pins and balls, everything pointed to a prosperous year, but we 
regret to report that in spite of these improvements the interest in 
Bowling has not been so keen with us as last year. 

We entered the team in the Intermediate Bowling League, and 
finished fourth. The Committee are already taking steps to pre- 
pare for an active season in the fall. 

The Club closed its season with a credit balance of $20.00. 


GEORGE A. ROSS, 
Chairman. 


SOCIAL DEPARTMENT 


The Social Department worked in conjunction with the other 
departments in an endeavor to meet the social needs of the 
members. This endeavor was supplemented by direct effort to 
reach a large number of men who joined for the social privileges 
only, and to this end social evenings were conducted in the fall 
months, and were largely successful and much appreciated by the 
new men whom we thus sought to acquaint with each other, and 
to interest in the Association. These evenings were discontinued 
in the New Year, and the members were directed to the 
Educational Talks held in the Social Parlors. 

The rearrangement and refurnishing of the Reception Hall and 
former Reading Room providing comfort, an opportunity to the 
members for self-entertainment, and a general air of spaciousness 
and good cheer contributed greatly to the end sought in our work. 
The rearrangement was carried out by a special committee. The 
cost was about $1,200. Towards this the Ladies’ Auxiliary have 
contributed $300, and there is still an open account for the con- 
tributions of members. The rooms were opened on December 10th, 
1907, and on that evening members contributed over $60.00. 

The Thanksgiving Tea was one of the most successful social 
functions ever held: The attendance was 140. 

The New Year’s Reception was conducted upon the plan adopted 
on previous occasions, with gymnastic exhibition in the afternoon, 
and concert in the evening. The attendance compared well with 
the best of other years. ‘ 

The Strangers’ Tea has been continued, and has again proved 
its value and confirmed its place in Association work. The 
sessions numbered 27, and 521 strangers were guests of the 
Association on these occasions. 

The Membership Committee might well report the evening they 
conducted with such success, for the entertainment and inspiration 
of the 150 new men brought into the membership by their special 
effort in the month of March, but we are glad to include it as one 
of the social events that will be long remembered by the guests of 
the evening. 


34 


The Lunch Room is becoming increasingly popular, and is 
proving itself worthy of the support it so well maintains, The 
general membership may be surprised to know that over 37,500 
customers have been served during the year. 


Respectfully submitted, 
ROBERT H. MACDONALD. 


SUMMER CAMP 


The Junior Camp was held in two sections, commencing June 
15th, the first two weeks for Business Boys, with 28 registered; 
the second, two weeks for the School Boys, with 41 and eight 
leaders, making a total attendance of 77. Mr. W. J. Holliday was 
in charge the entire time.

The Senior Camp opened on July 13th and closed September 3rd. 
Mr. W. H. Henderson was in charge the first two weeks, and Mr. 
C. BE. Reid the balance of the season. One hundred and twenty-one 
men were out, 16 less than last year.

Owing to bereavement in Mr. Paterson’s family, he was called 
to Montreal in December last, and we were favored with his 
presence during his stay here. He addressed several meetings in 
the Association, and presented some very interesting and encourag- 
ing details of his work. The Committee of Management also had 
the pleasure of taking tea with Mr. Paterson. 

The Foreign Work Committee and subscribers also had the 
pleasure of having tea with Mr. Gleason, and hearing a report on 
his work in Japan and during the Japanese-Russian war. Mr. 
Gleason also addressed a public meeting in the Association in the 
interests of the foreign work.

RAILROAD BRANCH 
POINT ST. CHARLES 


COMMITTEE OF MANAGEMENT 


Tuos. MCHATTIE, - - Chairman 
W. A. KNEELAND, B.C.L., - Vice-Chairman 
Dr. GEORGE HALL, - - Treasurer

EMPLOYED OFFICERS 


A. S. MCALISTER, - - - Secretary 
D. THOMSON, - - - Asst. Secretary 
H. B. ANDERSON, - - - Physical Director 


The splendid facilities provided for the boys and men of 
“Point St. Charles have been taken advantage of to a much 
ereater extent during the past year than formerly, and a spirit 
of optimism prevails generally. We are glad to report a grow- 
ing appreciation throughout the community at Point St. 
Charles for the work of the Association in all its Branches. 
This has been secured even under the disadvantage of the 
location of the building, and many other difficulties. 

We are able to report an increase of over 200 members for 
the year, the total membership now standing at 516. The 
receipts for the year were considerably in excess of what was 
anticipated, on account of changes that have been made in the 
building. They amount to $8,434, The amounts received from 
fees and room rents were also exceptionally large. 

We are able to report that $400 was paid on the old 
indebtedness, and all the eurrent obligations of the Branch 
met, as will be seen by the financial statement. In view of the 
financial stringeney which has prevailed, and especially the 
manner in which it has affected our community, we are thank- 
ful to be able to report this favorable financial result. 

Religious.—The religious work has shown a marked increase. 
Sunday Afternoon Meetings have been held throughout the 


37 


year with a good attendance, and 70 sessions for Bible study. 
This shows an increase over last year of 50 per cent. Noon- 
day Meetings for shop men have been held occasionally during 
the year. A special mission was conducted by Mr. A. G. 
Knebel, International Secretary, with marked success. A 
number of men publicly expressed a desire to lead the 
Christian life. The hospital visitation to railroad men has 
been continued throughout the year with great acceptance to 
those who have been laid aside by accident or illness. 

Educational_—The following subjects have been conducted : 
Shorthand, Bookkeeping, Air Brake, Standard Rules, 
Telegraphy, French, Mathematics, and Electricity. Three 
hundred and twenty-eight sessions were held, with an attend- 
ance of 2596. Practical Talks and Leetures were well 
attended. The results in the Educational Department show 
an increase of 100% over last year. 

Physical_—The securing of suitable ground for an athletic 
field from the Grand Trunk Railroad has held the members 
together during the summer. Seven clubs are now organized, 
Bowling, Basket-ball, Swimming, Baseball, Football, Lacrosse, 
and Harrier. Mr. H. B. Anderson, as Physical Director, has 
rendered good service to this department. Work for boys has 
been added with most encouraging results. 

Social.—Fifty-seven thousand meals were served in the 
Restaurant, which has continued to prove a very helpful 
feature. The dormitories have been well occupied during the 
whole year. The billiard tables and bowling alleys have 
greatly added to the social features of the Association, and 
have proved a special attraction to a large number of young 
men. They have provided means of amusement, and kept 
men from unfavorable surroundings. 

Mr. David Thomson succeeded Mr. J. S. Teet as Assistant 
Secretary. Tle has proved a very efficient member of the 
staff. The Committee of Management wish to place on record 
their appreciation of the service of their Seeretary, Mr. A. S. 
MeAllister, to whose energy and tact is due in large measure 
the suecess which has attended the work during the past year 


C. A. MANNING, 
Chairman.
